item.title: Population Age Structures of Countries
item.description: The age structures of populations vary considerably across countries. Some countries have relatively young populations, with large proportions consisting of children and adolescents. Other countries have much older age structures, with a substantial proportion of people aged 65 years or older. item.title: Nepal floods: Mounting death toll and concern for women and girls
item.description: As rescue efforts continue in Nepal, humanitarians are focused on how the recent deadly flash floods have impacted women and girls, as well as access to healthcare.

item.title: Food aid cutback in the occupied West Bank as health fears grow in Gaza
item.description: Lack of funding has forced the World Food Programme (WFP) to slash aid to families in the West Bank by half even though needs have more than doubled over the past two years.

item.title: Response must outpace spread of Ebola: UN relief chief
item.description: The world must move faster to contain an Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) that is growing exponentially, the UN’s Emergency Relief Coordinator warned on Tuesday.

item.title: At SCO summit In Kyrgyzstan, Guterres calls for more representative global governance
item.description: UN Secretary-General António Guterres on Tuesday urged leaders of the Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO) to help reshape global governance for a changing world, arguing that a more multipolar international order can strengthen multilateralism, advance fairness and better serve developing countries.

item.title: Decades of war have left ‘depth and breadth’ of trauma across Afghanistan, UN finds
item.description: Victims of Afghanistan’s decades-long armed conflict continue to suffer profound physical, psychological, social and economic consequences, often without access to justice, reparation or formal acknowledgement of the harm done to them, according to a new UN report.
